paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, dear sisters and elders. Today I had the privilege and blessing to visit with 20 of you amazing missionaries. I say amazing not to flatter you, but to hopefully help you see yourself a little more clearly than you might.

The very fact that you desired to go on a mission, the fact that you qualified to serve, and the fact that you're serving right now in this wonderful season of growth is complete and total evidence of your extraordinary position in the big picture of the second estate or the mortal probation. When you think of all the billions of people who have already lived and the billions that live now, you are in a very select and small group of chosen ones.
We see many examples in the scriptures where the Lord teaches us about our foreordained mission and the potential that he sees in us in hopes that we will choose.

To the prophet Jeremiah, the Lord declares his plan for him and his mission. In Jeremiah 1, verses four and five, we read, "then the word of the Lord came unto me saying, before I formed thee in the belly, I knew thee, and before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee and ordained thee a prophet unto the nations."

To the prophet Abraham, the Lord declared his past and his future. In Abraham 3:22-23, we read this. "Now the Lord had shown unto me Abraham the intelligences that were organized before the world was, and among all these were many of the noble and great ones, and God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said, these I will make my rulers, for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good, and he said unto me, Abraham, thou art one of them, thou wast chosen before thou wast born."
There are many revelations about the foreordained ministry of the prophet Joseph Smith. The one that I want to share with you, though, is important because it includes a very important warning.

In the Doctrine and Covenants, 3:1-5, we read. "The works and the designs and the purposes of God cannot be frustrated, neither can they come to naught. For God doth not walk in crooked paths, neither doth he turn to the right hand nor to the left, neither doth he vary from that which he hath said. Therefore his paths are straight and his course is one eternal round. Remember, remember, that it is not the work of God that is frustrated, but the work of men. For although a man may have many revelations and have power to do many mighty works, yet if he boasts in his own strength and sets at naught the counsels of God and follows after the dictates of his own will and carnal desires, he must fall and incur the vengeance of a just God upon him."
The Lord then goes on to reaffirm Joseph Smith's prophetic mission and that he can repent and get back on track with that, but he warns him again not to make that mistake again.
So let's talk about likening the scriptures to ourselves. How do we truly tap into and achieve our potential? How do we avoid making the terrible mistakes that lead us to lose our potential?
Let me explain by asking you some questions for you to think about and consider. Are you humble? Are you teachable? Are you responsive to the promptings of the spirit?

Now these sound like really simple questions and probably you all answered them, yes, yes, yes. But it's not that simple. You see, you're in a time of life when you're coming into your adulthood. You know, you're 20 years old or 18 years old or 25 years old. You're in a phase and a time where you're learning a little bit more about who you are but you've got to be making some really, really important decisions.

This is when you make the kinds of decisions that determine your destiny. It's so important as you understand that. Making a good choice literally can be the difference between happiness and misery, success and failure, prosperity and poverty, health and sickness and of course the really big choice which is will you fulfill your potential and do what you were sent here to do or slide down the course of least effort.

We each will make millions of choices in our lives but some choices really are more important than other choices because they are what I call keystone choices. A keystone choice is a choice that has a domino effect. A good keystone choice automatically brings about other good choices and a bad keystone choice automatically brings about other bad choices.

Here are some examples of keystone choices that are good. I choose to get up on time. And as a result I have more time to study and prepare and exercise. I choose to exercise and work hard all day and interestingly enough I'm tired when it's time to go to bed and also I go to sleep at 10 p.m. I choose to go to sleep at 10 p.m. I wake up at six because I'm rested and I'm ready to get up. I had a good eight hours of sleep.
Now that's just a little example but I think you get the point. A keystone choice positions you to make another good choice more easily.

Now my dear elders and sisters there are millions of keystone choices we can make but there is really only one keystone choice that will truly define us in the big picture. And that choice is between two ways of being. Now I want you to catch that. Two ways of being.
One way of being is to be receptive to the influence of the Holy Spirit. The other way is to be resistant to the influence of the Holy Spirit.

In every moment of our lives we are actually making this critically important choice. We make it over and over again. We get a little prompting say you're sorry. We get a little prompting do something nice for someone. We get a little prompting get up so you can study. We get a little prompting and all of those promptings are from the Holy Spirit. And when we're responsive we get up. We act on it. We say the kind word. We apologize. We repent. We forgive. We do that responsive thing that the Spirit whispers to us to do.

If we are resistant to the Spirit we'll have those promptings but we'll resist them. We'll say I don't want to do that. I don't like that person. That person was mean to me or I don't feel very good or I didn't get that much sleep or I don't want to study that right now. It's boring.

You see you're having a conversation inside your own head as you're either responding to the Spirit or being resistant to the Spirit. And I want to tell you that this is the big choice. This is the big question that you have to deal with every moment of your day.

And if you get in the habit of literally being responsive to the Spirit. Now I'm not perfect in this for sure. None of us really are. But as we get better and better at it what happens is we find ourselves just making really awesome choices. And we look back over our day or back over our week and we're saying, oh I'm glad I did that. I didn't really want to do it. I didn't really want to say that. I didn't really want to repent or forgive or act on that or do that video to that family or do that certain thing that helps somebody else. I was too tired. I was too this or whatever, but I did it. I was responsive and because I was responsive not only did I feel good after but look what good came from it. It really changed their situation. They're more hopeful and happy.

You see when we're proud, when we feel like we know everything already, when we feel like that somebody's not treating us right and we should be treated better, when we have all that natural man in us what happens is we just naturally become very resistant to the Spirit.

But when we're humble, when we're teachable, when we see everyone around us with more patience and kindness what happens is we naturally are responsive to the Spirit and we are thereby quote, "led by the Spirit," close quote. And since the Spirit, quote, "knoweth all things," close quote, we are led to make incredibly intelligent choices that bring about the best possible outcomes in our lives.

When we're resistant to the Spirit we are quote, "left unto ourselves," close quote. To rely on our own strength and our own wisdom and no matter how smart you are and I know there's, every one of you are super smart but the fact of the matter is you're not smarter than the Holy Spirit. And you're not smart enough to navigate this crazy world we live in as effectively and as successfully as you would if you were being led by the Spirit.

So I'd like to encourage each of you to become more aware of and sensitive to the promptings of the Spirit. To do this will require a humility and a meekness that you may find difficult at first. It will require a commitment to keeping the commandments a little more faithfully than you may have in the past. It will require a little more diligence and a little more precision and preparation in your planning and in your execution of your plans.
All of the attributes of Christ are important just because they're the attributes of Christ. But their greatest value is their power to help you be responsive to the Holy Spirit.

So elders and sisters, please give it your best effort this week to see if you don't make a lot better choices and enjoy a better outcome to your week as you are responsive to the promptings of the Spirit.

I love you elders and sisters. Sister Hughes loves you as well. Please enjoy your evening. And here's how you can enjoy it the best. Do something that makes someone else feel more hope, more happiness and more faith. You have the power and you are foreordained to be here right now to do it. God bless you.
